title: Add prefix cache reuse histograms (reuse depth + reused tokens) with prompt-length buckets
author: Samir Qureshi
commits: runtime/metrics: add prefix cache reuse histograms + prompt length bucketing
runtime/cache: expose reuse stats from prefix cache lookup path (no prompt logging)
telemetry: add label allowlist + unit tests for bucket mapping
docs: add metric definitions + examples to internal metrics README
description: Summary: Introduces prefix cache reuse histograms to make cache effectiveness actionable beyond a single hit-rate number. We emit two histograms per request (sampled) tagged with coarse request shape (prompt length bucket) and a small, allowlisted set of context labels. Metrics are designed to be low overhead and safe for production ingestion (no raw prompt content; no per-request IDs). Motivation: Hit/miss counters tell us whether we found something, but not whether the reuse was meaningful. In production we see many partial reuses (e.g., small shared prefixes) that still incur large prefill cost. These histograms quantify (1) how deep into the prompt we reused and (2) how many prefill tokens were avoided by reuse. This helps Runtime/SRE diagnose regressions and enables the recommendations job to suggest canonicalization / routing locality / cache sizing. Metric definitions (per request, recorded after prefill decision): 1) redwood.cache.prefix.reuse_depth_tokens (histogram) = number of initial prompt tokens served from prefix cache (0 for miss). 2) redwood.cache.prefix.reused_prefill_tokens (histogram) = estimated number of prefill tokens avoided due to prefix reuse (0 for miss). Labels (controlled): - model_family (allowlist; e.g. llama, mistral, qwen) - deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private) - region (coarse region code already in runtime context) - prompt_len_bucket (bucketed; see below) Notes: We intentionally do NOT include tenant_id, route_id, request_id, or model_version in these histograms to avoid series explosion. Route/model version slicing stays with the counter-based metrics and traces, per the cardinality policy discussed with Telemetry. Prompt length bucketing: prompt_len_bucket is computed from prefill prompt token count. Buckets are fixed edges to make dashboards stable and avoid per-model drift: [0-128], [129-256], [257-512], [513-1024], [1025-2048], [2049-4096], [4097-8192], [8193+]. Implementation details: - The prefix cache lookup returns (hit, reused_tokens) and a conservative estimate of prefill tokens avoided. The avoided estimate is computed from (reused_tokens, tokenizer-normalized prompt token count) without inspecting raw prompt text. - We register histograms via the runtime metrics registry and record them only when cache telemetry is enabled (config flag) and when sampling passes (see sampling note below). - Histograms are recorded at most once per request, with the recording occurring after the request has a stable prompt token count to avoid batched prefill double-counting. Testing: - Added unit tests for bucket assignment boundary conditions and label allowlists. - Added a runtime integration test that drives repeated prompts and asserts reuse_depth_tokens increases on subsequent calls (with prefix caching enabled). - Bench sanity: instrumentation is behind the cache_telemetry flag and sampled; local microbench showed no measurable p95 delta at 1% sampling (numbers in ENG-4821 notes). Sampling/overhead: - Default sampling for histograms is 1% (configurable) since histograms are heavier than counters. Counters/hit-rate remain unsampled. - Recording path avoids allocations; labels are precomputed from interned strings where possible. Rollout plan: - Ship disabled by default; enable in staging for 24h, then canary 5% prod for 48h, then 100% if ingestion cost + perf canary are stable. - Dashboard panels will be added in observability-pack (separate PR) once the histograms are visible in prod. Known limitations: - reused_prefill_tokens is an estimate; it is intended for trend analysis and correlating to wasted prefill, not as a billing-grade number. - For streaming retries, recording is guarded by request attempt semantics; we do not emit multiple histogram samples for the same logical request attempt. Review notes: Aligns with the cache-metrics naming and cardinality policy and ADR semantics (partial reuse is expected; 0 values are valid and meaningful).
review_conversation:
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we clarify the semantic difference between reuse_depth_tokens vs reused_prefill_tokens? They look correlated; worried dashboards will misinterpret. Also please confirm we don’t emit model_version label on histograms.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added a short definition block + example in docs. Confirmed no model_version/route_id/tenant_id labels on the histograms; only model_family + deployment_mode + region + prompt_len_bucket.

Nadia Rahman (review): Metric names should match standards: use redwood.cache.prefix.* prefix and avoid “saved” wording; also please ensure prompt_len_bucket uses the shared bucketing helper so edges are consistent across runtime + gateway.
Samir Qureshi (author): Renamed metrics to redwood.cache.prefix.reuse_depth_tokens and redwood.cache.prefix.reused_prefill_tokens. Switched to common/telemetry bucket helper and added tests for boundary values.

Caleb Johnson (review): Any chance model_family can explode? Please enforce allowlist and map unknown to “other”. Also want a hard cap on label values to prevent ingestion-side drops.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added allowlist mapping with fallback “other” and a unit test. Label values are all static enums; prompt_len_bucket comes from fixed edges.

Allison Grant (review): Please add one paragraph in the PR description about how SRE should interpret a drop in reuse_depth but stable hit-rate (workload drift vs eviction). This will help when we build dashboards.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added guidance in docs and PR description. In short: stable hit-rate with lower reuse depth usually indicates shorter common prefixes (prompt canonicalization regression or changed prompt template), whereas hit-rate drop + eviction pressure points to cache sizing/pressure.

Noah Patel (review): Minor: watch for recording twice when prefill is batched. I see you moved recording to after prompt token count stabilizes; add a regression test comment.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added comment + adjusted integration test to cover the ‘batched prefill’ path by forcing continuous batching in the test harness.

Approvals: Omar El-Sayed approved. Nadia Rahman approved. Caleb Johnson approved. Allison Grant approved.
